units.title: Sentence structure & word order
units.intro: English is S-V-O. Tigrinya is S-O-V, so keep the verb as a middle anchor and use an overt copula.

cards.title: S-V-O vs S-O-V
rule: English declarative order is **Subject–Verb–Object**.
Tigrinya is **Subject–Object–Verb**; putting the English verb last is a common L1 error.
Keep the main verb as a **middle anchor** after the subject.

examples.text: The guard locked the gate at midnight.
The guard the gate locked at midnight.
examples.fix: The guard locked the gate at midnight.

cards.title: Copula and clause boundaries
rule: English needs an overt copula (*is/are/was/were*) between subject and complement.
Do not join two independent clauses with only a comma (comma splice).
Use a full stop, semicolon, or a conjunction (*and/but/so/because*).

examples.text: It rained; therefore we stayed in.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Find the subject, then check that a finite verb follows immediately — never leave the verb at the end.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Use S-V-O, place the copula after the subject, and close clause boundaries without comma splices.

tips.text: Find the subject, then check that a finite verb follows immediately — never leave the verb at the end.

Identify the sentence that contains a copula verb

options.A: The security guard the main gate locked at midnight.
options.B: The security guard locked the main gate at midnight.
options.C: At midnight the security guard the main gate locked.
options.D: Locked the security guard the main gate at midnight.

why: Answer B: The security guard locked the main gate at midnight.
English requires a strict Subject-Verb-Object ($$\text{S-V-O}$$) pattern. The subject is 'The security guard', the verb is 'locked', and the direct object is 'the main gate'.

Option A and Option C place the verb ('locked') at the end of the clause, which is an $$\text{S-O-V}$$ pattern typical of Tigrinya grammar (ሓላው ሰላም ማዕጾ ዓጸዎ) and represents a common L1 transfer error. Option D incorrectly places the verb before the subject without an auxiliary in a declarative statement.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.label: 2. Identify the sentence that contains a copula verb error caus

Choose the sentence that correctly manages sentenc

options.A: She is an excellent English teacher.
options.B: They are very proud of their exam results.
options.C: My brother a hardworking farmer in the village.
options.D: We were delighted to receive your letter.

why: Answer C: My brother a hardworking farmer in the village.
Every English sentence expressing a state of being requires an explicit copula verb ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were') between the subject and the predicate nominative.

In Option C, the copula verb 'is' is completely missing. In Tigrinya, the copula can sometimes be omitted or structurally merged, leading students to translate "ሓወይ ኣብቲ ዓዲ ትጉህ ሓረስታይ [እዩ]" directly as "My brother a hardworking farmer..." without including the essential English copula 'is'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

Complete the sentence with the correct word order:

options.A: The rain was heavy, we decided to stay indoors.
options.B: The rain was heavy we decided to stay indoors.
options.C: The rain was heavy; therefore, we decided to stay indoors.
options.D: Because the rain was heavy, so we decided to stay indoors.

why: Answer C: The rain was heavy; therefore, we decided to stay indoors.

A comma splice occurs when two independent clauses are joined with only a comma. Option A is a comma splice. Option B is a run-on sentence. Option C uses a semicolon and a conjunctive adverb ('therefore'), which is structurally perfect.

Option D is a double-conjunction error ('Because... so...'). Tigrinya speakers often use both because they translate morphological markers like "ስለዝ-... ስለዚ..." directly into English. Option C correctly separates the clauses.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

Which of the following ditransitive sentences is g

options.A: yesterday welcomed the new students warmly
options.B: warmly welcomed the new students yesterday
options.C: welcomed yesterday warmly the new students
options.D: the new students welcomed warmly yesterday

why: Answer B: warmly welcomed the new students yesterday

English adverbs of manner ('warmly') usually precede the main verb or follow the object. Adverbs of time ('yesterday') belong at the end of the sentence. The correct structure is: Subject ('The school principal') + Adverb of Manner ('warmly') + Verb ('welcomed') + Object ('the new students') + Adverb of Time ('yesterday').

Option D shows $$\text{S-O-V}$$ word order. Option A places the time adverb ('yesterday') between the subject and the verb, which is acceptable in Tigrinya but highly irregular and awkward in English unless formatted as a fronted adverbial.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

Identify the sentence that has a word order error

options.A: The grandmother told a beautiful story her grandchildren.
options.B: The grandmother told to her grandchildren a beautiful story.
options.C: The grandmother told her grandchildren a beautiful story.
options.D: The grandmother her grandchildren a beautiful story told.

why: Answer C: The grandmother told her grandchildren a beautiful story.

Ditransitive verbs ('tell', 'give', 'buy') can take two structures: $$\text{S} + \text{V} + \text{Indirect Object (IO)} + \text{Direct Object (DO)}$$ OR $$\text{S} + \text{V} + \text{DO} + \text{to/for} + \text{IO}$$.

Option C follows the $$\text{S-V-IO-DO}$$ pattern ('her grandchildren' is IO, 'a beautiful story' is DO). Option A lacks the preposition 'to' which is required if DO comes before IO. Option D is an $$\text{S-O-V}$$ trap.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

options.A: He is not a member of the organizing committee.
options.B: They are not ready to take the national examination.
options.C: She is a doctor not in this public hospital.
options.D: We are not satisfied with the current classroom conditions.

why: Answer C: She is a doctor not in this public hospital.
In English, negative copular sentences follow the structure: $$\text{Subject} + \text{Copula} + \text{not} + \text{Complement}$$.

Option C places 'not' after the predicate noun phrase ('a doctor not...'). In Tigrinya, negation is prefixed and suffixed to the copula at the end (ንሳ ኣብዚ ዶክተር ኣይኮነትን), which can lead students to misplace the negative particle in English.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

similar.q: Which of the following sentences exhibits the corr

options.A: Although the storm damaged many homes, the community rebuilt quickly.
options.B: The storm damaged many homes, but the community rebuilt quickly.
options.C: The storm damaged many homes the community rebuilt quickly.
options.D: The storm damaged many homes; the community rebuilt quickly.

why: Answer C: The storm damaged many homes the community rebuilt quickly.
A run-on sentence occurs when two independent clauses are joined without any punctuation or coordinating conjunctions.

Option C strings 'The storm damaged many homes' and 'the community rebuilt quickly' together with zero punctuation. Tigrinya speakers, used to inflectional markers on verbs for clausal relationships, often overlook the strict English requirement for punctuation boundaries or conjunctions.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Select the sentence with the correct placement of multiple adverbials.
questions.label: 8. Select the sentence with the correct placement of multiple a

similar.q: Identify the sentence that contains a copula verb

options.A: The athlete ran in the stadium gracefully this morning.
options.B: The athlete ran gracefully this morning in the stadium.
options.C: The athlete ran gracefully in the stadium this morning.
options.D: This morning the athlete ran in the stadium gracefully.

why: Answer C: The athlete ran gracefully in the stadium this morning.
When multiple adverbials modify a single verb, English follows the sequence: Manner (How) $$\rightarrow$$ Place (Where) $$\rightarrow$$ Time (When).

In Option C: 'gracefully' (Manner), 'in the stadium' (Place), and 'this morning' (Time) are correctly sequenced ($$\text{M} \rightarrow \text{P} \rightarrow \text{T}$$). Other options violate this standard order, which is a frequent target in matric grammar tasks.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Identify the grammatical error in the sentence: 'My cousin he bought a new car last week.'
questions.label: 9. Identify the grammatical error in the sentence: 'My cousin h

similar.q: Choose the sentence that correctly manages sentenc

options.A: The adverb of time 'last week' is at the end.
options.B: There is a double subject ('My cousin' and 'he').
options.D: The direct object 'a new car' is misplaced.

why: Answer B: There is a double subject ('My cousin' and 'he').
In English, a noun subject must not be followed immediately by its corresponding pronoun subject in the same clause. This creates a redundant double subject.

In Tigrinya, verbs are conjugated with pronominal suffixes that match the subject (e.g., ወዲ ሓወይ መኪና ዓዲጉ - where the verb contains the subject marker). Direct translation often causes students to state the subject and then immediately repeat it with a pronoun ('My cousin he...').
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Choose the correct question word order for an information search (Wh-question).
questions.label: 10. Choose the correct question word order for an information se

similar.q: Complete the sentence with the correct word order:

options.A: Where you did buy that beautiful traditional dress?
options.B: Where did you buy that beautiful traditional dress?
options.C: Where you bought that beautiful traditional dress?
options.D: You bought that beautiful traditional dress where?

why: Answer B: Where did you buy that beautiful traditional dress?
English Wh-questions with active verbs require subject-auxiliary inversion: $$\text{Wh-word} + \text{Auxiliary Verb (do/does/did)} + \text{Subject} + \text{Base Verb} + \text{Object}$$.

Option B correctly inverts 'did' and 'you'. Option A and Option C are common L1 transfer errors where the speaker maintains standard declarative word order ($$\text{Wh-word} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

units.title: Subject–verb agreement
units.intro: The verb must agree with its true subject in number, even when phrases come between them.

cards.title: Basic agreement
rule: Singular subject → singular verb: *The exam **starts** at eight.*
Plural subject → plural verb: *The exams **start** at eight.*
A phrase between subject and verb does not change agreement: *The box of books **is** heavy.*

examples.text: The list of names is long.
The list of names are long.
examples.fix: The list of names is long.

cards.title: Tricky cases
rule: *each / every / everybody* → singular.
*either … or / neither … nor* → agree with the nearer noun.
Collective nouns may be singular when the group acts as one.

examples.text: Neither the teachers nor the principal was late.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Ignore prepositional phrases after the subject; agree with the head noun.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Singular subjects take singular verbs; plural subjects take plural verbs; watch collective and either/or.

tips.text: Ignore prepositional phrases after the subject; agree with the head noun.

questions.q: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high school graduates ________ the rising cost of higher education.
questions.label: 1. One of the most challenging obstacles facing high school gra

similar.q: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high
The board of directors, despite having conflicting

why: The subject of the sentence is 'One' (singular) in the pattern $$\text{One of} + \text{Plural Noun} + \text{Singular Verb}$$. The plural noun phrase 'the most challenging obstacles' is part of a prepositional phrase modifying the subject.
Students often match the verb to the plural noun 'obstacles' which is closest to the verb slot, leading them to choose 'are' (Option A). This is a classic attraction trap in matriculation exams.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The board of directors, despite having conflicting opinions on the new expansion policy, ________ finally agreed on the budget.
questions.label: 2. The board of directors, despite having conflicting opinions

similar.q: The board of directors, despite having conflicting
Neither the regional program coordinator nor the s

why: The subject is 'The board' (singular collective noun). The phrase 'of directors' and the parenthetical clause 'despite having conflicting opinions...' are intervening elements that do not change the subject's singular number.

Students are often distracted by the plural nouns 'directors' and 'opinions' and select the plural auxiliary 'have' (Option B). Isolating the subject 'The board' reveals that the singular 'has' is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

The local police ________ currently searching the

why: The compound subject is connected by the correlative conjunction 'Neither... nor'. The proximity rule applies, meaning the verb agrees with the closer subject, 'the senior researchers' (plural).

Students may focus on 'the coordinator' (singular) and choose 'was' (Option A). The past time marker 'yesterday' eliminates present auxiliaries 'is' and 'are', leaving 'were' (Option B) as the correct choice.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

Mathematics ________ always been regarded as a fou

why: 'Police' is a collective noun that is always plural in English and must be paired with plural verbs.

Because 'police' does not end in '-s', students often assume it is singular and choose 'is' (Option A) or 'was' (Option C). The time marker 'currently' indicates present tense, which makes 'are' (Option B) correct.

questions.label: 5. Mathematics ________ always been regarded as a foundational

similar.q: Mathematics ________ always been regarded as a fou
Three thousand dollars ________ too much to pay fo

why: Academic subjects ending in '-ics' (mathematics, physics, politics) look plural because of the '-s' suffix, but they are singular uncountable nouns. The perfect auxiliary 'been' requires 'has' or 'have'.
Students are often tricked by the '-s' at the end of 'Mathematics' and select 'have' (Option B). This is a common spelling-appearance trap on ESSLCE exams.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Three thousand dollars ________ too much to pay for a second-hand water pump in this small town.
questions.label: 6. Three thousand dollars ________ too much to pay for a second

similar.q: Three thousand dollars ________ too much to pay fo
One of the most challenging obstacles facing high

why: Nouns representing specific quantities of money, time, distance, or weight are treated as a single, collective unit ($$\text{Quantity} \rightarrow \text{Singular Verb}$$).
Students see the plural noun 'dollars' and choose 'are' (Option A) or 'were' (Option C). However, because the amount is treated as a single sum, it requires the singular verb 'is' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Not only the students but also their instructor ________ highly motivated to complete the laboratory project before the semester ends.
questions.label: 7. Not only the students but also their instructor ________ hig

similar.q: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high

why: The compound subject is connected by 'not only... but also'. The verb must agree with the closer subject, which is 'their instructor' (singular).

Students may choose the plural 'are' (Option B) because they see both 'students' and 'instructor' and assume the subject must be plural. The proximity rule requires the singular verb 'is' (Option A) to match the singular 'instructor'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Some of the milk in the larger containers ________ spoiled, so we must discard it immediately.
questions.label: 8. Some of the milk in the larger containers ________ spoiled,

similar.q: The board of directors, despite having conflicting

why: 'Some' belongs to the SANAM variable category. Its grammatical number is determined by the noun in the modifying prepositional phrase: 'of the milk'. Since 'milk' is uncountable (singular), 'Some' is singular.
Students may look at 'containers' (plural) and select a plural verb like 'have' (Option B) or 'are' (Option C). The correct auxiliary is 'has' (Option A) to match the uncountable noun 'milk'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The soccer team ________ currently putting on their individual uniforms in the locker room.
questions.label: 9. The soccer team ________ currently putting on their individu

similar.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the s

why: 'Team' is a collective noun. The context 'putting on their individual uniforms' shows that the members are acting as separate individuals, which requires a plural verb.
Students often assume collective nouns are always singular and choose 'is' (Option B). The use of the plural possessive pronoun 'their' confirms that the verb must be plural 'are' (Option A).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Every single book, including the rare historical manuscripts in the library vault, ________ cataloged last year.
questions.label: 10. Every single book, including the rare historical manuscripts

similar.q: The local police ________ currently searching the

why: 'Every single book' is the subject of the sentence. The indefinite modifier 'Every' is singular. The phrase 'including the rare historical manuscripts...' is an intervening phrase that does not affect the subject's singular number.

Students often choose 'were' (Option B) or 'are' (Option C) because they match the verb to the plural 'manuscripts' or 'vault'. The past time marker 'last year' requires the singular past verb 'was' (Option A).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

units.title: Modals & semi-modals
units.intro: Modals (*can, must, should, might…*) express ability, obligation, advice and possibility without *to*.

cards.title: Core modals
rule: **must / have to** = obligation; **should / ought to** = advice.
**can / could** = ability or permission; **may / might** = possibility.
Modal + bare infinitive: *You should revise.*

cards.title: Perfect modals
rule: **must have + V3** = logical conclusion about the past.
**should have + V3** = past advice / regret.
**could have + V3** = past possibility that did not happen.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: After a modal use the bare infinitive: must go, not must to go.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Choose the modal for meaning (obligation vs advice vs possibility) and keep the bare verb after it.

glossary.meaning: helping verb of mood: can, must, should…

tips.text: After a modal use the bare infinitive: must go, not must to go.

questions.q: I failed the national biology matriculation exam; I ________ harder instead of wasting my time on social media.
questions.label: 1. I failed the national biology matriculation exam; I ________

similar.q: I failed the national biology matriculation exam;
According to the laboratory safety rules, you ____

why: The context 'I failed...; I [blank] harder' indicates a past regret or criticism of an action that was advisable but did not happen. This requires the past regret modal structure ($$\text{should have} + \text{V}_3$$).

Students often confuse 'must have studied' (logical deduction of fact) with 'should have studied' (regret). Option A implies the speaker is deducing that they studied, which contradicts 'I failed'. Option B is correct because it expresses regret.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: According to the laboratory safety rules, you ________ enter the chemistry room without wearing safety goggles.
questions.label: 2. According to the laboratory safety rules, you ________ enter

similar.q: According to the laboratory safety rules, you ____
Aster has been studying and living in London for t

why: The context describes a strict laboratory safety rule. This requires a modal of prohibition to show the action is forbidden ($$\text{must not} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).

Students often confuse 'don't have to' (lack of obligation/optional) with 'must not' (prohibition/forbidden). Option A would incorrectly imply that wearing goggles is optional, which violates safety rules. Option B is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.label: 3. Aster has been studying and living in London for ten years,

similar.q: Aster has been studying and living in London for t
The soccer field is completely covered in puddles;

why: The context presents strong present evidence ('living in London for ten years'). This requires a modal of present logical deduction to show high certainty ($$\text{must} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
Students sometimes choose 'must have' (Option D), but 'must have' is for past deduction ($$\text{must have} + \text{V}_3$$) and cannot be followed by the base verb 'speak'. Option A is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The soccer field is completely covered in puddles; it ________ heavily during the night.
questions.label: 4. The soccer field is completely covered in puddles; it ______

similar.q: The soccer field is completely covered in puddles;
The main classroom door was heavily jammed, but th

why: The present evidence 'The soccer field is completely covered in puddles' leads to a strong positive deduction about a past event. This requires 'must have' ($$\text{must have} + \text{V}_3$$).

Students often confuse 'should have rained' (past regret/unrealized advice) with 'must have rained' (past deduction of fact). Option A is incorrect because we are deducing a fact based on physical evidence, making Option B correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The main classroom door was heavily jammed, but the strong security guard ________ open it for us.
questions.label: 5. The main classroom door was heavily jammed, but the strong s

similar.q: The main classroom door was heavily jammed, but th
Tomorrow is a national public holiday, so we _____

why: This sentence describes a specific, successful action in a past situation. This requires 'was able to' or 'managed to' ($$\text{Subject} + \text{was/were able to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).

Students often choose 'could' (Option A) because they translate it as past ability. However, 'could' is only used for general past ability, while specific past successes require 'was able to' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Tomorrow is a national public holiday, so we ________ wake up early to attend classes.
questions.label: 6. Tomorrow is a national public holiday, so we ________ wake u

similar.q: Tomorrow is a national public holiday, so we _____
I failed the national biology matriculation exam;

why: The context describes a lack of obligation or necessity because tomorrow is a holiday (it is optional to wake up early). This requires 'don't have to' ($$\text{don't have to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
Students often choose 'must not' (Option A) because they confuse prohibition with a lack of obligation. Option B is correct because waking up early is not forbidden; it is simply not required.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The river water was contaminated with waste; we ________ drunk it without boiling it first.
questions.label: 7. The river water was contaminated with waste; we ________ dru

similar.q: I failed the national biology matriculation exam;

why: The context 'The river water was contaminated... we [blank] drunk it' indicates a past criticism or regret of an action that did happen but was undesirable. This requires 'shouldn't have' ($$\text{shouldn't have} + \text{V}_3$$).
Option A 'must not have' is grammatically incorrect for past logical deduction or regret in standard English. Option B is correct because it expresses regret for a completed past action.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: He ________ stolen the library books yesterday; he was with me in the seminar hall all afternoon.
questions.label: 8. He ________ stolen the library books yesterday; he was with

similar.q: According to the laboratory safety rules, you ____

why: The context provides strong negative evidence ('he was with me... all afternoon'). This requires a modal of past logical deduction to show negative certainty ($$\text{can't have} + \text{V}_3$$).

Students often try to use 'must not have' to show negative certainty, which is incorrect. In English, 'can't have' (Option B) is the correct past negative equivalent of 'must have' to show that a past action was impossible.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Every student should ________ to the lecture hall on time to secure a seat.
questions.label: 9. Every student should ________ to the lecture hall on time to

similar.q: Aster has been studying and living in London for t

why: Core modal verbs like 'should' must strictly be followed by a bare infinitive verb ($$\text{Modal} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).

Students often make the error of inserting 'to' after 'should', choosing 'to come' (Option A), or adding participle suffixes, choosing 'coming' (Option B). Only the bare infinitive 'come' (Option C) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: You have a severe cough; you ________ see the doctor before your condition gets worse.
questions.label: 10. You have a severe cough; you ________ see the doctor before

similar.q: The soccer field is completely covered in puddles;

why: The context describes strong, urgent advice with a negative consequence if ignored ('before your condition gets worse'). This requires the semi-modal 'had better' ($$\text{had better} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
Option C 'ought' is incorrect because it lacks 'to'. Option D 'have to' shows external obligation but is less natural for urgent, cautionary advice. Option A is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

units.title: Active and passive voice
units.intro: Passive = be + past participle. Use it when the receiver matters more than the doer.

cards.title: Forming the passive
rule: Active S-V-O → Passive: object becomes subject + **be + V3** (+ by-agent).
Tense of be matches the active tense: writes→is written; wrote→was written.
Do not omit be: *The bridge was built*, not *The bridge built*.

examples.text: The gate is locked every night.

cards.title: Progressive and perfect passives
rule: Progressive: *is being cleaned*.
Perfect: *has been signed*.
Future: *will be completed* / *will have been completed*.

examples.fix: The room is being painted. / has been painted.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: If the subject is inanimate and cannot perform the action, expect a passive.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Form passives with the correct be-tense + V3; do not drop be (L1 trap).

glossary.meaning: be + past participle; subject receives the action

tips.text: If the subject is inanimate and cannot perform the action, expect a passive.

questions.q: The official report on the regional economic development ________ by the committee before the deadline last night.
questions.label: 1. The official report on the regional economic development ___

similar.q: The official report on the regional economic devel
A massive amount of money ________ currently _____

why: The subject 'The official report' is inanimate and cannot perform the action of submitting. This requires the passive voice. The time-marker 'last night' indicates the Simple Past tense, requiring the past passive form ($$\text{was/were} + \text{V}_3$$).

Students often choose the active form 'submitted' (Option A) due to direct translation, or 'has been submitted' (Option C), which is present perfect and cannot be paired with the definite past time-marker 'last night'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: A massive amount of money ________ currently ________ to fund the construction of the new school library.
questions.label: 2. A massive amount of money ________ currently ________ to fun

similar.q: A massive amount of money ________ currently _____
The high school teacher ________ a beautiful tradi

why: The subject is 'A massive amount of money' (singular and inanimate), requiring the passive voice. The time-marker 'currently' indicates an action in progress, requiring the Present Progressive Passive ($$\text{is/are} + \text{being} + \text{V}_3$$).
Students often choose 'is raising' (Option A) because they confuse active and passive progressive forms. Since 'money' cannot raise itself, the passive 'is being raised' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The high school teacher ________ a beautiful traditional gift by the students on her graduation day.
questions.label: 3. The high school teacher ________ a beautiful traditional gif

similar.q: The high school teacher ________ a beautiful tradi
The national examination papers ________ by next F

why: This is a double-object passive where the Indirect Object 'The high school teacher' is placed in the subject position: $$\text{IO} + \text{be} + \text{V}_3 + \text{DO}$$.

Students often choose 'gave' (Option A) because they see a person as the subject and assume the active voice. However, the context shows she received the gift, requiring the passive form 'was given' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The national examination papers ________ by next Friday afternoon, according to the official schedule.
questions.label: 4. The national examination papers ________ by next Friday afte

similar.q: The national examination papers ________ by next F
The legendary king of Axum ________ to have built

why: Answer B: will have been printed

The inanimate subject 'examination papers' requires the passive voice. The time-marker 'by next Friday' indicates a future point of completion, requiring the Future Perfect Passive ($$\text{will have been} + \text{V}_3$$).

Students often see 'next Friday' and choose active 'will print' (Option A) or active future perfect 'will have printed' (Option D). Because papers cannot print themselves, the passive 'will have been printed' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The legendary king of Axum ________ to have built several stone obelisks during his reign.
questions.label: 5. The legendary king of Axum ________ to have built several st

similar.q: The legendary king of Axum ________ to have built
A prestigious academic scholarship ________ to Daw

why: This is an impersonal passive reporting structure using the subject-infinitive pattern: $$\text{Subject} + \text{be} + \text{V}_3 + \text{to-infinitive}$$.

Students often choose active 'believes' (Option A) or progressive 'is believing' (Option D). Since the king does not believe himself, but people believe *about* him, the passive 'is believed' (Option B) is required.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: A prestigious academic scholarship ________ to Dawit because of his outstanding ESSLCE results.
questions.label: 6. A prestigious academic scholarship ________ to Dawit because

similar.q: A prestigious academic scholarship ________ to Daw
The official report on the regional economic devel

why: This is a double-object passive where the Direct Object 'A prestigious academic scholarship' is the subject: $$\text{DO} + \text{be} + \text{V}_3 + \text{to} + \text{IO}$$.
Students often choose 'awarded' (Option B) because they assume the active past tense. However, a scholarship cannot award itself, making the passive 'was awarded' (Option A) correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The historic church in the village ________ in the 14th century, but historians are still researching its origin.
questions.label: 7. The historic church in the village ________ in the 14th cent

similar.q: The official report on the regional economic devel

why: The subject 'The historic church' is inanimate. The definite past time-marker 'in the 14th century' strictly requires the Past Simple passive ($$\text{was/were} + \text{V}_3$$).
Students often choose 'has been built' (Option A) because they see it as a permanent present state. Definite historical dates require the simple past passive 'was built' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: It ________ that the ancient city of Adulis was a prosperous port for international trade.
questions.label: 8. It ________ that the ancient city of Adulis was a prosperous

similar.q: A massive amount of money ________ currently _____

why: This is an impersonal passive reporting structure using the introductory 'It' pattern: $$\text{It} + \text{be} + \text{V}_3 + \text{that-clause}$$.
Students often choose active 'reports' (Option A) or 'reported' (Option C) because they translate directly from Tigrinya. The formal English reporting structure requires 'It is reported' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Several modern research laboratories ________ in our school since the regional budget was increased.
questions.label: 9. Several modern research laboratories ________ in our school

similar.q: The high school teacher ________ a beautiful tradi

why: The time-marker 'since' indicates an action that started in the past and continues to the present, requiring the Present Perfect Passive ($$\text{have/has been} + \text{V}_3$$).

Students often choose active 'have established' (Option A) or simple past passive 'were established' (Option C). Because the laboratories were established by someone, and 'since' requires a perfect tense, Option B is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: While the laboratory experiments ________ by the science students, the principal walked in to inspect the rooms.
questions.label: 10. While the laboratory experiments ________ by the science stu

similar.q: The national examination papers ________ by next F

why: 'While' introduces an ongoing background action in the past, requiring the Past Continuous. The subject 'experiments' is inanimate, requiring the Past Progressive Passive ($$\text{was/were being} + \text{V}_3$$).
Students often choose active 'were conducting' (Option A). However, experiments cannot conduct themselves, so the passive 'were being conducted' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

units.title: Reported speech
units.intro: Reported speech shifts tense and pronouns when the reporting verb is past.

cards.title: Backshift basics
rule: Direct: *“I am ready,” she said.* → Reported: *She said (that) she was ready.*
will → would; can → could; have done → had done.
*tell* needs a person object: *He told me to wait.*

examples.text: She said she is tired yesterday.

cards.title: Forms and examples
head: Direct
Reported
rows: She told me to stay there.

cards.title: Questions and commands
rule: Yes/No: *asked if/whether* + clause (no do-support).
Wh-questions: keep the wh-word; use statement order.
Commands: *told/asked + object + to-infinitive*.

examples.text: She asked if I was ready.

examples.fix: She asked if I was ready.

examples.text: He told us to sit down.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Backshift: present→past, past→past perfect, will→would; keep place/time words consistent.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Use told + person, said (that)…; adjust tense when the reporting verb is past.

glossary.meaning: moving tenses one step back in reported speech

tips.text: Backshift: present→past, past→past perfect, will→would; keep place/time words consistent.

questions.q: The director asked me ________ to the project meeting scheduled for the next morning.
questions.label: 1. The director asked me ________ to the project meeting schedu

similar.q: The director asked me ________ to the project meet
The school principal warned the students ________

why: Answer B: whether I would come

This is a reported Yes/No question. It requires the complementizer 'if' or 'whether', followed by declarative word order ($$\text{if/whether} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$). Because the reporting verb 'asked' is past, the future 'will' must backshift to 'would'.
Option C and Option D incorrectly invert the subject and auxiliary. Option A fails to backshift 'will' to 'would'. Only Option B correctly implements both backshifting and declarative word order.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The school principal warned the students ________ inside the laboratory compound.
questions.label: 2. The school principal warned the students ________ inside the

similar.q: The school principal warned the students ________
She told me that she ________ her university appli

why: This is a reported negative command. Negative commands are reported using the structure: $$\text{reporting verb} + \text{object} + \text{not to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

Students often place the negative particle 'not' after 'to' (Option A), resulting in 'to not run', which is a common split-infinitive error. Option B is correct because 'not' must strictly precede 'to'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: She told me that she ________ her university application the day before.
questions.label: 3. She told me that she ________ her university application the

similar.q: She told me that she ________ her university appli
The police officer asked the driver where ________

why: The time-marker 'the day before' indicates that the original speech contained the Simple Past ('yesterday'). In reported speech with a past reporting verb, Simple Past must backshift to Past Perfect ($$\text{Simple Past} \rightarrow \text{Past Perfect}$$).

Students often choose Simple Past 'submitted' (Option A), failing to apply the backshifting rule. Present perfect 'has submitted' (Option B) is incorrect because it cannot represent a completed past action in reported speech.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The police officer asked the driver where ________ his car during the morning rush hour.
questions.label: 4. The police officer asked the driver where ________ his car d

similar.q: The police officer asked the driver where ________
The biology teacher stated that plants ________ su

why: This is a reported Wh-question. It must follow declarative word order ($$\text{Wh-word} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$). Because the original question was in the past tense ('Where did you park?'), the verb must backshift to Past Perfect.
Option A and Option C incorrectly maintain interrogative inversion. Option B 'he had parked' correctly uses declarative word order and the backshifted Past Perfect tense.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The biology teacher stated that plants ________ sunlight to manufacture their food.
questions.label: 5. The biology teacher stated that plants ________ sunlight to

similar.q: The biology teacher stated that plants ________ su
Dawit says that he ________ ready to take the nati

why: The reported statement describes a scientific fact (general truth). General truths are an exception to the backshifting rule and remain in the Simple Present tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).
Students blindly apply backshifting to 'needed' (Option A) because they see the past reporting verb 'stated'. This is a common conceptual trap on national exams.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Dawit says that he ________ ready to take the national examination next month.
questions.label: 6. Dawit says that he ________ ready to take the national exami

similar.q: Dawit says that he ________ ready to take the nati
The director asked me ________ to the project meet

why: The reporting verb 'says' is in the Present Simple. When the reporting verb is in the present, no backshifting is applied to the reported clause.
Students often automatically backshift to 'was' (Option B) because they assume all reported speech is past. Option A 'is' is correct because the reporting verb is present.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: She asked me why ________ her the previous night as we had agreed.
questions.label: 7. She asked me why ________ her the previous night as we had a

similar.q: The director asked me ________ to the project meet

why: This is a reported negative Wh-question. It must follow declarative word order ($$\text{Why} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$). Because 'the previous night' indicates a past action, the verb must backshift to Past Perfect.
Option A and Option D incorrectly maintain subject-auxiliary inversion. Option B 'I hadn't called' correctly uses declarative word order and the backshifted Past Perfect tense.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The administrative assistant ________ that the registration office was temporarily closed.
questions.label: 8. The administrative assistant ________ that the registration

similar.q: The school principal warned the students ________

why: The reporting verb is followed directly by a *that*-clause. The verb 'said' does not require a personal object, whereas 'told' must be followed by a personal object ($$\text{Subject} + \text{said} + \text{that-clause}$$).

Option A and Option D are incorrect because 'told' requires a personal object ('told me'). Option B is incorrect because 'say' cannot be followed directly by a personal object without 'to'. Option C is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: He wanted to know how many candidates ________ for the regional examination.
questions.label: 9. He wanted to know how many candidates ________ for the regio

similar.q: She told me that she ________ her university appli

why: This is a reported Wh-question. The original question 'How many candidates have registered/registered?' must backshift to the Past Perfect ($$\text{S} + \text{had} + \text{V}_3$$) because the reporting verb 'wanted to know' is past.
Students often choose 'did register' (Option B) or 'have registered' (Option C), failing to apply backshifting. Option A is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The suspect admitted that he ________ the national archive building the night before.
questions.label: 10. The suspect admitted that he ________ the national archive b

similar.q: The police officer asked the driver where ________

why: The time-marker 'the night before' indicates that the original speech contained the Simple Past. In reported speech with a past reporting verb, Simple Past must backshift to Past Perfect.
Students often choose Simple Past 'entered' (Option A), failing to apply the backshifting rule. Past Perfect 'had entered' (Option C) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

units.title: Conditionals & wish
units.intro: Match if-clause and result tenses: 0/1 real, 2 unreal present, 3 unreal past, mixed for past→present.

cards.title: Types 0–3
rule: 0: If + present, present (facts).
1: If + present, will + V (real future).
2: If + past, would + V (unreal now); prefer *were*.
3: If + past perfect, would have + V3 (unreal past).

examples.text: If it rains, we will stay in.
If it will rain, we will stay in.
examples.fix: If it rains, we will stay in.

examples.text: If I were you, I would apply.

cards.title: Forms and examples
head: Type
Form
rows: If + had + V3, would have + V3

cards.title: Mixed conditionals and wish
rule: Past cause → present result: *If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.*
Wish + past = present regret; wish + past perfect = past regret.
Inverted forms: *Had I known…*, *Were I you…*, *Should you need…*.

examples.text: If she had trained, she would be fitter now.
I wish I had prepared yesterday.

examples.fix: I wish I had prepared yesterday.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Never put would in the if-clause of type 2/3; use were for formal type 2.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Zero/first for facts and real futures; second/third for unreal present/past; wish uses unreal past forms.

glossary.meaning: if and result refer to different times

tips.text: Never put would in the if-clause of type 2/3; use were for formal type 2.

games.title: Match the form to its example

pairs.b: If + had + V3, would have + V3

questions.q: If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Celsius, water automatically turns into ice.
questions.label: 1. If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Celsius, wate

similar.q: If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Cel
If I ________ you, I would accept the administrati

why: This sentence describes a scientific fact (general truth), requiring the Zero Conditional structure: $$\text{If} + \text{Present Simple}, \text{Present Simple}$$.

Students often choose 'will drop' (Option A) because they assume all conditionals require 'will' in the result. However, for absolute scientific certainties, both clauses must strictly remain in the Present Simple. 'The temperature' is singular, so 'drops' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: If I ________ you, I would accept the administrative job offer without any hesitation.
questions.label: 2. If I ________ you, I would accept the administrative job off

similar.q: If I ________ you, I would accept the administrati
Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier

why: This is a Second Conditional sentence expressing an unreal, hypothetical situation in the present ('I would accept').

In formal academic English, the subjunctive **were** must be used for all subjects (including I, he, she, it) in Second Conditional 'if' clauses. Choosing 'was' (Option A) is a common colloquial trap on exams. Option B is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier, they ________ the valuable documents from the fire.
questions.label: 3. Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier, they ___

similar.q: Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier
I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now;

why: The sentence begins with the inverted auxiliary 'Had' ('Had the rescue team arrived...'), which is an inverted Third Conditional structure ($$\text{Had} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_3 \dots$$). The main clause must use the formula: $$\text{would have} + \text{V}_3$$.
Students are often confused by the lack of 'if' at the beginning of the sentence. Recognizing 'Had... arrived' as an inverted conditional makes the correct choice 'would have saved' (Option B) clear.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now; I wish I ________ more free time to rest.
questions.label: 4. I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now; I wish I _

similar.q: I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now;
Aster ________ sick today if she hadn't eaten that

why: The context 'now' and 'I am extremely busy' indicates a present regret (unreal present). Present regrets using 'wish' require the Past Simple tense in the subordinate clause ($$\text{Subject} + \text{wish} + \text{Subject} + \text{Past Simple}$$).

Students often choose 'have' (Option A) because they see 'now'. However, because the wish is about an unreal present situation (I wish I had time, but I don't), the Past Simple 'had' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Aster ________ sick today if she hadn't eaten that contaminated street food yesterday.
questions.label: 5. Aster ________ sick today if she hadn't eaten that contamina

similar.q: Aster ________ sick today if she hadn't eaten that
Unless you ________ studying English grammar daily

why: This is a Mixed Conditional sentence. The condition is in the past ('if she hadn't eaten... yesterday'), but the result is in the present ('today'). This past-present connection requires the formula: $$\text{If} + \text{Past Perfect}, \text{would} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

Students often blindly choose 'would not have been' (Option A) because they see 'hadn't eaten' in the 'if' clause. However, the present result marker 'today' requires the mixed conditional form 'would not be' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Unless you ________ studying English grammar daily, you will not achieve a high score on the ESSLCE.
questions.label: 6. Unless you ________ studying English grammar daily, you will

similar.q: Unless you ________ studying English grammar daily
If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Cel

why: The conjunction 'Unless' means 'if... not' and carries a negative meaning. The First Conditional formula requires: $$\text{Unless} + \text{Present Simple}, \text{will not} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

Because *unless* is already negative, you cannot use a negative verb like 'don't start' (Option A) in the *unless* clause. This double-negative trap is highly tested on exams. Option B 'start' is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: I spent all my money on clothes last week; if only I ________ more careful with my budget.
questions.label: 7. I spent all my money on clothes last week; if only I _______

similar.q: If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Cel

why: The context 'last week' indicates a past regret. Regrets about past events using 'if only' strictly require the Past Perfect tense ($$\text{If only} + \text{Subject} + \text{Past Perfect}$$).

Students are often confused by the phrase 'if only' and treat it like 'wish'. Past regrets require the Past Perfect 'had been' (Option C) rather than the subjunctive 'were' (Option B), which is for present regrets.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: ________ you see the program supervisor tomorrow, please tell him that I have finished the report.
questions.label: 8. ________ you see the program supervisor tomorrow, please tel

similar.q: If I ________ you, I would accept the administrati

why: This is an inverted First Conditional sentence. The word 'if' is omitted, and the modal 'should' is fronted ($$\text{Should} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_{\text{base}} \dots$$ is equivalent to $$\text{If} + \text{Subject} + \text{Present Simple}$$).

Students often choose 'Had' (Option A) or 'Were' (Option B). However, 'Had' is for third conditional inversion and 'Were' is for second conditional. 'Should' (Option C) is the correct auxiliary for first conditional inversion.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: If we ________ more trees in our urban areas, the air quality would improve significantly.
questions.label: 9. If we ________ more trees in our urban areas, the air qualit

similar.q: Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier

why: The main clause uses 'would improve' ($$\text{would} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$), which indicates a Second Conditional structure. The 'if' clause must strictly use the Past Simple tense ($$\text{If} + \text{Past Simple}$$).
Students often choose 'plant' (Option A) because they see it as a present possibility. However, to match 'would improve', the past tense 'planted' (Option B) is grammatically required.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: I wish you ________ playing that loud music; I cannot concentrate on my exam preparation.
questions.label: 10. I wish you ________ playing that loud music; I cannot concen

similar.q: I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now;

why: The speaker is expressing annoyance and a desire for someone else's behavior to change in the future. This requires the structure: $$\text{Subject} + \text{wish} + \text{Subject} + \text{would} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

Students often choose 'stopped' (Option B) because they confuse this with a present regret. However, when expressing annoyance about someone else's current behavior, 'would stop' (Option C) is grammatically required.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

units.title: Gerunds, infinitives & participles
units.intro: Some verbs take -ing, some take to-infinitive; prepositions take -ing.

cards.title: Verb patterns
rule: enjoy/avoid/suggest/finish + -ing.
want/decide/hope/plan + to-infinitive.
stop + -ing = quit; stop + to-V = pause in order to.

cards.title: Adjective + infinitive; preposition + -ing
rule: easy/hard/important + to-infinitive.
good at / interested in / before + -ing.
look forward to + -ing (*to* is a preposition here).

examples.text: She is interested in studying history.
I look forward to meet you.
examples.fix: I look forward to meeting you.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: After a preposition always use a gerund: interested in learning.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Memorise high-frequency patterns; stop + -ing ≠ stop + to-infinitive.

tips.text: After a preposition always use a gerund: interested in learning.

questions.q: The driver of the school bus managed to avoid ________ the pedestrian on the narrow mountain road.
questions.label: 1. The driver of the school bus managed to avoid ________ the p

similar.q: The driver of the school bus managed to avoid ____
We are extremely looking forward to ________ the h

why: The lexical verb 'avoid' belongs to the category of verbs that must strictly govern a gerund: $$\text{avoid} + \text{Gerund}$$.
Students often choose 'to hit' (Option A) due to direct translation of infinitival thoughts. Option B 'hitting' is the correct gerund form required by 'avoid'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: We are extremely looking forward to ________ the historical obelisks of Axum during our school holidays.
questions.label: 2. We are extremely looking forward to ________ the historical

similar.q: We are extremely looking forward to ________ the h
I clearly remember ________ the laboratory door, b

why: In the phrasal verb 'look forward to', 'to' functions as a preposition, not an infinitive marker. Therefore, it must strictly be followed by a gerund ($$\text{look forward to} + \text{V-ing}$$).

Students almost always fall for the trap of choosing 'visit' (Option A) or 'to visit' (Option C) because they see 'to'. This is a high-frequency prepositional trap on national exams. Option B is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: I clearly remember ________ the laboratory door, but I should double-check to be absolutely sure.
questions.label: 3. I clearly remember ________ the laboratory door, but I shoul

While walking to the school library, he stopped __

why: The context 'but I should double-check to be sure' shows that the locking happened in the past, and the speaker now has a memory of it. This past memory requires a gerund: $$\text{remember} + \text{Gerund}$$.
Students often confuse 'remember to lock' (future duty) with 'remember locking' (past memory). Since the locking was already performed, 'locking' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: While walking to the school library, he stopped ________ some traditional bread from the local bakery.
questions.label: 4. While walking to the school library, he stopped ________ som

similar.q: While walking to the school library, he stopped __
Despite the heavy rain and road blockages, we mana

why: The context shows that the speaker interrupted his walk *in order to* buy bread. This purpose or reason requires a to-infinitive: $$\text{stop} + \text{to-infinitive}$$.
Students often confuse 'stop to buy' (pause to do) with 'stop buying' (quit the habit). Since he paused his walk to perform the action, 'to buy' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Despite the heavy rain and road blockages, we managed ________ at the examination hall on time.
questions.label: 5. Despite the heavy rain and road blockages, we managed ______

similar.q: Despite the heavy rain and road blockages, we mana
She is highly interested in ________ biochemistry

why: The verb 'manage' strictly governs a to-infinitive: $$\text{manage} + \text{to-infinitive}$$.
Students often choose 'arriving' (Option A) thinking it fits the progressive sense of the sentence. Only the to-infinitive 'to arrive' (Option B) is grammatically correct after 'manage'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: She is highly interested in ________ biochemistry when she joins the national university next year.
questions.label: 6. She is highly interested in ________ biochemistry when she j

similar.q: She is highly interested in ________ biochemistry
The driver of the school bus managed to avoid ____

why: The adjective phrase 'interested in' contains the preposition 'in'. All prepositions must be followed strictly by gerunds: $$\text{Preposition} + \text{Gerund}$$.
Students are often tempted to choose 'to study' (Option B) because they translate "ክተጽንዕ" directly. Prepositional phrases strictly require 'studying' (Option A).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: ________ his final examination papers, Dawit quietly walked out of the hall to rest.
questions.label: 7. ________ his final examination papers, Dawit quietly walked

similar.q: The driver of the school bus managed to avoid ____

why: The sentence describes two past actions in chronological sequence: first, finishing the exam, and second, walking out. This requires a perfect participle clause: $$\text{Having} + \text{V}_3 \dots$$.
Option A 'Finishing' implies the actions were happening at the exact same time, which is logically incorrect. Option B 'Having finished' correctly indicates the prior completion of the first action.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: ________ down the narrow street, the old university library suddenly appeared on our left.
questions.label: 8. ________ down the narrow street, the old university library

similar.q: We are extremely looking forward to ________ the h

why: Answer C: While we were walking
If we use 'Walking' (Option A), the subject of the main clause ('the old university library') becomes the logical subject of walking, creating a dangling modifier error (the library cannot walk).

Students often choose 'Walking' (Option A) because they fail to check subject-matching. Option C 'While we were walking' correctly provides an explicit subject ('we'), resolving the dangling modifier.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The candidate strongly objected to ________ the additional registration fee for the examination.
questions.label: 9. The candidate strongly objected to ________ the additional r

similar.q: I clearly remember ________ the laboratory door, b

why: In 'object to', 'to' is a preposition. Therefore, it must be followed by a gerund ($$\text{object to} + \text{V-ing}$$).
Students see 'to' and choose 'pay' (Option A) or 'to pay' (Option C), falling into the infinitive trap. The phrasal verb requires 'paying' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The suspect persistently denied ________ the secure university archive room last night.
questions.label: 10. The suspect persistently denied ________ the secure universi

similar.q: While walking to the school library, he stopped __

why: The verb 'deny' belongs to the class of verbs that strictly govern a gerund: $$\text{deny} + \text{Gerund}$$.
Students often choose 'to enter' (Option A) due to L1 translation. Only the gerund 'entering' (Option B) is correct after 'deny'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

units.title: Cohesive devices
units.intro: Connectors show addition, contrast, cause and purpose — and each class has its own grammar.

cards.title: Contrast and purpose
rule: although/even though + S + V.
despite/in spite of + noun / V-ing.
so that + S + modal; in order to + Vbase.

examples.fix: Despite studying, he failed. / Although he studied, he failed.

examples.text: He revised so that he could pass.

cards.title: Conjunctive adverbs
rule: therefore/however/moreover link clauses with ; … ,
Do not write Because… so… or Although… but… (double conjunction).
Match meaning: therefore=result, however=contrast, moreover=addition.

examples.text: Although she tried, but she failed.
The roads were blocked; however, buses ran.

cards.title: Common mistakes
head: Wrong
Right
Why
rows: Although he was late… / Despite being late…

cards.title: Memory tip
body: although + clause; despite + noun/gerund; so that + clause; in order to + base verb.

body: Pick the connector for the logic and for the structure that follows the blank.

questions.q: ________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the administrative staff arrived at the school on time.
questions.label: 1. ________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the administrat

similar.q: ________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the a
The final chemistry revision class was canceled __

why: The blank is followed by a noun phrase 'the heavy storm and road blockages' (no verb present) and introduces contrast. This requires a noun-governing concessive preposition: $$\text{despite / in spite of} + \text{Noun Phrase}$$.
Students often choose 'Although' (Option A) or 'Even though' (Option C) because they translate 'እኳ እንተ-... ምስ' similarly. Option D 'In spite' is incorrect because it lacks 'of'. Option B is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The final chemistry revision class was canceled ________ the sudden illness of the professor.
questions.label: 2. The final chemistry revision class was canceled ________ the

similar.q: The final chemistry revision class was canceled __
Although the laboratory equipment was extremely ex

why: The blank is followed by a noun phrase 'the sudden illness of the professor', indicating a cause-and-effect relationship. This requires a prepositional cause marker: $$\text{because of} + \text{Noun Phrase}$$.

Students often choose 'because' (Option A) or 'since' (Option C) because they translate both as 'ስለ...'. However, 'because' requires a full clause ($$\text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$), while 'because of' (Option B) is correct for noun phrases.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Although the laboratory equipment was extremely expensive, ________ we decided to purchase it for our research.
questions.label: 3. Although the laboratory equipment was extremely expensive, _

similar.q: Although the laboratory equipment was extremely ex
She studied hard until midnight ________ she could

why: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction at the beginning of the sentence to connect the clauses. In English, only one conjunction can connect two clauses; adding a second is a double-conjunction error.
Students often choose 'but' (Option A) because in Tigrinya, it is natural to pair concession with contrast (e.g., 'ድኻ እኳ እንተኾነ፡ ግን...'). Option D is correct because no extra connector is allowed.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: She studied hard until midnight ________ she could pass the national biology examination.
questions.label: 4. She studied hard until midnight ________ she could pass the

similar.q: She studied hard until midnight ________ she could
________ being extremely tired after the long jour

why: The blank is followed by a full clause containing a modal verb ('she could pass...'). This requires a clause-based purpose connector: $$\text{so that} + \text{Subject} + \text{modal} + \text{Verb}$$.

Students often choose 'in order to' (Option A) or 'so as to' (Option C) because they translate both as 'ምእንቲ'. However, those infinitive-based connectors require a bare verb ($$\text{in order to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$), making Option B correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: ________ being extremely tired after the long journey, she completed her chemistry homework.
questions.label: 5. ________ being extremely tired after the long journey, she c

similar.q: ________ being extremely tired after the long jour
He studied the grammar modules diligently; _______

why: The blank is followed by a gerund 'being' (no subject present) and introduces contrast. This requires a noun-governing concessive preposition: $$\text{in spite of} + \text{Noun/V-ing}$$.

Students often choose 'Although' (Option A) or 'Even though' (Option C) because they translate 'being tired' as a clause. Since there is no subject before 'being', the prepositional 'In spite of' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: He studied the grammar modules diligently; ________, he achieved a top score on the ESSLCE.
questions.label: 6. He studied the grammar modules diligently; ________, he achi

similar.q: He studied the grammar modules diligently; _______
________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the a

why: The blank is preceded by a semicolon and followed by a comma, indicating a conjunctive adverb is required. The logical relationship is cause-and-effect (result).

Students often choose 'furthermore' (Option C) because it has the same punctuation. However, 'furthermore' indicates addition, while the logical context requires 'consequently' (Option A - as a result) to show the effect of his study.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: We will not be able to finish the project on time ________ everyone works much harder.
questions.label: 7. We will not be able to finish the project on time ________ e

similar.q: ________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the a

why: The sentence expresses a negative condition: we won't finish *unless* (if not) everyone works harder. This requires the negative conditional conjunction 'unless' ($$\text{unless} = \text{if} + \text{not}$$).

Students often choose 'if' (Option A) because they translate 'እንድሕር' directly. However, using 'if' would mean 'if everyone works harder, we won't finish', which is logically incorrect. Option B 'unless' is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: He woke up early in the morning ________ arrive at the regional examination hall on time.
questions.label: 8. He woke up early in the morning ________ arrive at the regio

similar.q: The final chemistry revision class was canceled __

why: The blank is followed by a bare verb 'arrive', indicating a purpose relationship. This requires an infinitive-based purpose connector: $$\text{so as to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.
Students often choose 'so that' (Option A) because they translate it as 'ምእንቲ'. However, 'so that' requires a full clause ($$\text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$), making 'so as to' (Option B) correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The newly bought computer is very cheap; ________, its performance is excellent for research.
questions.label: 9. The newly bought computer is very cheap; ________, its perfo

similar.q: Although the laboratory equipment was extremely ex

why: The blank is preceded by a semicolon and followed by a comma. The logical relationship is contrast: the computer is cheap (negative/neutral) but its performance is excellent (positive).

Students often choose 'moreover' (Option A) or 'therefore' (Option C) because they see the semicolon and comma. However, the contrastive context requires 'however' (Option B - yet/but) to show the opposing ideas.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Aster prefers studying physics, ________ her younger sister loves biology.
questions.label: 10. Aster prefers studying physics, ________ her younger sister

similar.q: She studied hard until midnight ________ she could

why: The sentence compares two differing preferences directly (contrast), requiring a subordinating conjunction of contrast: $$\text{Clause}_1 + \text{whereas} + \text{Clause}_2$$.

Students often choose 'furthermore' (Option B) because they think it connects ideas, or 'despite' (Option C) which requires a noun phrase. Option A 'whereas' is correct because it directly contrasts two clauses.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.
